p: I was hired by Nosey, a clothing and skate brand, to develop a custom T-shirt design and video intro. This project gave me the opportunity to explore a grunge-inspired creative direction, blending streetwear culture with bold pop aesthetics. I wanted to capture the raw, expressive nature of skate culture while maintaining a distinctive visual identity that reflected the brand’s personality.

I was commissioned to create a custom T-shirt design for a Kingdom Hearts fan. As someone who personally loves the game's aesthetic and artistic style, this was an exciting opportunity to blend my own creativity with its iconic visuals. I incorporated grunge textures, bold illustrations, and streetwear-inspired graphics to create a unique piece. Featured here is the final mockup presented to my client, a design I genuinely enjoyed bringing to life.

My creative direction was focused on capturing the energy and intricate visual style of Kingdom Hearts. I had a lot of fun experimenting with shading, form, and composition to create a dynamic and expressive design. By incorporating bold graphics, detailed illustrations, and grunge-inspired elements, I wanted to create a piece that felt alive while staying true to the game's iconic aesthetic.

I was contacted by an old high school friend who had recently completed his military service. He noticed a gap in the apparel market for military-inspired clothing that felt more like an authentic streetwear brand rather than traditional military merchandise. He also felt that his particular branch of service lacked representation in the clothing industry. With this vision in mind, he reached out to me to help establish a distinctive visual identity and bring his brand to life through bold, expressive designs.

My creative direction was focused on bringing a sense of realism to a stylized, cartoon-inspired design. I wanted the artwork to feel authentic, expressive, and full of movement. My goal as a designer is always to create work that feels lived-in and alive, with a strong sense of character and energy. That is what makes art so meaningful to me, and I strive to carry that passion into every design I create.

h2: S.O.S  Son Of Saints Gym Culture Brand
p: Sons of Saints (SOS) is a fitness and lifestyle brand built around discipline, self-improvement, and community. The brand approached me to capture its founder and entrepreneur through engaging video content that would generate hype, build brand awareness, and inspire others to embrace a healthier lifestyle.

My creative direction focused on capturing the energy, passion, and authenticity behind the brand. Through dynamic cinematography, intentional editing, and visual storytelling, I wanted to create content that did more than promote working out. I wanted to motivate viewers, establish an emotional connection, and encourage them to become part of the Sons of Saints culture.
The overall goal was to showcase SOS as more than just a fitness brand, but as a movement centered around becoming the best version of yourself.

I was contracted by Gabriel Mora, owner of Mora’s Pest Control, to develop creative media, advertisements, and an elevated logo design that would strengthen his brand identity and help his business reach a broader audience.

My approach to video production was to take an informative subject like pest control and make it entertaining, approachable, and easy to understand. Through fun creative concepts, clean editing, and a relaxed delivery, I developed video content that showcased Gabriel’s expertise while allowing his personality to shine through.

The overall goal was to move away from traditional, overly scripted advertisements and create an authentic viewing experience that people could connect with. I wanted to help Gabriel spread awareness of his services, build trust with potential customers, and establish a memorable brand presence through engaging and digestible content.

Lunchboxx is a content-driven automotive brand centered around two friends documenting the process of rebuilding and bringing their project truck to life. I was commissioned to create a highly detailed, original piece of artwork that captured their personality, automotive passion, and grunge aesthetic while translating seamlessly into a wearable T-shirt design.

My creative direction focused on bold linework, vibrant colors, rugged textures, and intricate mechanical details. I incorporated elements of their project truck, equipment, and surroundings to create a personalized illustration that tells a story and reflects the authentic identity behind Lunchboxx.

Rather than creating a traditional merchandise graphic, I wanted to develop a collectible piece of art that their audience would genuinely enjoy wearing. This project showcases my attention to detail, digital illustration abilities, and understanding of how to translate a brand's personality into visually distinctive merchandise.
I was tasked with creating the pilot episode for Mixed Bag, an ongoing animated cartoon series that currently features two episodes and a Christmas special.
This project gave me the opportunity to explore a different creative medium and bring an entertaining concept to life through animation, humor, and visual storytelling.

My creative direction was focused on embracing artistic freedom and showcasing my understanding of different genres, entertainment styles, and audience engagement. I wanted to create something fun, expressive, and memorable while stepping outside the boundaries of traditional brand advertisements and commercial media.

This project represents the more playful and artistic side of my creative abilities. It demonstrates my versatility as a content creator and my ability to develop engaging content across multiple mediums, social media platforms, and entertainment formats.

p: This was the first concept that came to mind when exploring the idea of creating a Monster Energy-inspired brand project. My goal was to capture and reinterpret the brand's recognizable aesthetic while incorporating my own artistic approach.

My goal was to capture and reinterpret the brand's recognizable aesthetic while incorporating my own artistic approach. I wanted to demonstrate how adaptable my design style can be while staying true to the identity and visual language of an established brand.
I created the entire packaging design and its visual assets from scratch, with the goal of exploring how Monster Energy's recognizable brand identity could translate into a popsicle product.

I wanted to establish a color palette that felt both recognizable and familiar to Monster Energy's existing brand identity. I drew inspiration from two of the brand's most iconic flavors, Original Monster and Ultra White, because of their recognizable packaging and strong presence in the product lineup.

I focused on combining dark grays, black, white, and Monster's signature green to maintain the brand's bold and aggressive aesthetic.

For the font I wanted to go with something that was a bit more edgy to fit in with the aesthetic of Monster as a brand. I used PF Fuel Decay as the font and I think it brough to life the entire package.

p: Gabriel Mora is a one-man powerhouse running his own pest control business, serving communities throughout Lake Elsinore, Menifee, and the surrounding areas. He reached out to me for a logo redesign, giving me the opportunity to develop a refreshed visual identity that reflects his hardworking personality, professionalism, and dedication to his business.

Take his existing logo to the next level. My objective was to elevate his visual identity, creating something more personalized, polished, and professional while preserving the original character of his brand and reflecting the quality of his work.

My creative direction focused on taking what worked in the original logo and elevating it into a more polished, visually engaging identity. I incorporated a vibrant gradient, a refined background, and insect silhouettes to visually communicate the services his company provides. To add a personal touch, I incorporated his own likeness into the design, making the logo feel more authentic and connected to the individual behind the business. I also prioritized typography that was bold, eye-catching, and easily readable without compromising the overall composition.

With Gabriel Mora specializing in rodent and insect extermination, I wanted to i= the advertisement from an unexpected perspective: the pests themselves. Creative ideas like this often come naturally to me, and I enjoy capitalizing on those spontaneous moments of inspiration. My goal was to bring that concept to life through humor, visual storytelling, and an unconventional approach that makes the advertisement both engaging and memorable.

I went for a military style font to go with the vibe of extermination and reference to the ants go marching song. I picked the colors synonymous with his brand to pop out. This was taken on my Camera and edited in Photoshop and Adobe Illustrator.
I just wanted to showcase the original design before I had gotten
to editing and updating it. I changed the background, the font, and
the overall orientation of the original flow of the design. I wanted to
add him to it because he is the face of the brand and is who people
are going to see when he comes to do work on their house, company
I wanted to capture Gabe in his work truck to capture his brands energy.
